OK, got it~

[TopN](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/21163/files#diff-d1ffc678be7b676d586bca576ae7a9dab715d233bc88249c522f2f9e7ef69660) is such a case. And I think we can always pre-allocate the `[]Row` like the following, to ensure a better performance when using `chunk.AppendRows()`

```go
func BenchmarkBatchAppendRows(b *testing.B) {
	...
	for _, conf := range testCaseConfs {
		...
		b.ResetTimer()
		rows := make([]Row, 0, conf.batchSize) // pre-allocate `rows` to reduce memory allocation overhead.
		b.Run(fmt.Sprintf("column-%d", conf.batchSize), func(b *testing.B) {
			rows = rows[:0]
			for i := 0; i < conf.batchSize; i++ {
				rows = append(rows, rowChk.GetRow(i))
			}
			for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ {
				chk.Reset()
				chk.AppendRows(rows)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

issue_context.title: hptc ycsb-worloade: Implement AppendRows for Chunk
issue_context.body:
## Description

This is a issue when viewing the profile of ycsb-workloade, i.e. `select * from t where key > ? and limit = ?`.

While the task it self may be batched, the appending process is not. In distsql.go:

```
for resultTask.cursor < len(resultTask.rows) {
    req.AppendRow(resultTask.rows[resultTask.cursor])
    resultTask.cursor++
```

`AppendRow` eventually goes to (utils/chunk/chunk.go):

```
for i, rowCol := range row.c.columns {
    chkCol := c.columns[colOff+i]
    appendCellByCell(chkCol, rowCol, row.idx)
}
```

So, the result is that, tidb is accessing columns in different memory locations every time appending a new row, which is not cache-friendly. And it gets worse when the scanning is large(large `maxscanlength` in ycsb worload parameter).

The task is to:
1. write `AppendRows` by a loop of columns of chunk, that is appending one column of one chunk until all rows of the corresponding column are exausted, then next column of rows, on and on...
2. a benchmark to show the improvement
3. a test to verify the correctness.

## Score

- 300

- @xhebox
